ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a triangular path, and the problem states that it is an equilateral triangle. The arrows show that the ant walks upward along the left side, labeled with a speed of 5 cm/min; walks downward along the right side, labeled with a speed of 15 cm/min; and walks leftward along the bottom side, labeled with a speed of 20 cm/min. Then reason: Because the triangle is an equilateral triangle, the three side lengths are equal. Let each side length be s cm, then the total distance the ant walks around the whole triangle is 3s. The total time is s/5 + s/15 + s/20. Putting over a common denominator gives 1/5 + 1/15 + 1/20 = 12/60 + 4/60 + 3/60 = 19/60, so the total time is 19s/60. The average speed is total distance divided by total time, namely 3s / (19s/60) = 180/19 cm/min.

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram: it shows an equilateral triangular path with the ant moving up the left side at 5 cm/min, down the right side at 15 cm/min, and left along the bottom side at 20 cm/min. From the text, use that the triangle is equilateral, so the three side lengths are equal. Let each side have length s cm. Compute total distance as 3s and total time as s/5 + s/15 + s/20. Then average speed/velocity around the full trip is total distance divided by total time: 3s / (s/5+s/15+s/20), cancel s, and simplify to 180/19 cm/min.
